rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When considering God as He is, without treating oneness as a separate predicate, the mind reaches unity; the same distinction answers objections about existence and necessity.
rows.anchor: لكن فرق بين النظر إليه من حيث أنه هو وبين النظر إليه من حيث أنه محكوم عليه بأنه واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No affirmation or negation can describe the divine essence without introducing something distinct; bare هو points toward the beginnings of tawhid.
rows.anchor: لا يمكن التعبير عنه لأنك متى عبرت عنه فقد أخبرت عنه بأمر آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Oneness meaning simple numerical unity is not unique to God, since contingent beings include individuals and composites that depend on simples.
rows.anchor: المركب لا بد فيه من المفردات فثبت أنه لا بد من إثبات المفردات في عالم الممكنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone has the distinctive oneness of having no partner in necessary existence; al-Razi points to the proof from 21:22.
rows.anchor: ليس في الوجود شيء يشاركه في وجوب الوجود

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i calls God one in four respects: without parts, uniquely eternal, uniquely divine, and unique in essential attributes.
rows.anchor: الجبائي : يوصف الله تعالى بأنه واحد من وجوه أربعة

rows.speaker: أبو هاشم
rows.claim: Abu Hashim gives three respects, combining God's uniqueness in eternity with uniqueness in essential attributes.
rows.anchor: أبو هاشم يقتصر على ثلاثة أوجه : فجعل تفرده بالقدم ، وبصفات الذات وجها واحدا

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qadi says this verse intends God's exclusive divinity, since it explicitly follows the oneness claim with no deity but Him.
rows.anchor: القاضي : وفي هذه الآية المراد تفرده بالإلهية فقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi's school affirms that God is one in essence without an equal, in attributes without likeness, and in acts without a partner.
rows.anchor: أصحابنا : إنه سبحانه وتعالى واحد في ذاته لا قسيم له ، وواحد في صفاته لا شبيه له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second divine individual would need a differentiating addition, making the essence composite, contingent, caused, and dependent; therefore God is one in essence.
rows.anchor: فإن كان الأول كان امتياز ذاته المعينة عن المعنى الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Created beings receive their attributes from another, whereas God has His attributes from Himself, distinguishing His attributes from theirs.
rows.anchor: كل ما عداه فان ، لأن حصول صفاته له لا تكون من نفسه بل من غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Created attributes belong to one time rather than another because they arise in time, while God's attributes are not temporal in that way.
rows.anchor: صفات غيره مختصة بزمان دون زمان لأنها حادثة ، وصفات الحق ليست كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's attributes are unlimited in their objects: His knowledge encompasses all knowables and His power all possibles.
rows.anchor: فإن علمه متعلق بجميع المعلومات وقدرته متعلقة بجميع المقدورات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's essence is neither a substrate for attributes nor perfected by additions; rather, its own completeness entails attributes of perfection.
rows.anchor: ولا أيضا بحسب كون ذاته مستكملة بها لأنا بينا أن الذات كالمبدأ لتلك الصفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human reason cannot know the quiddity of God's attributes or essence, but infers them through their observable effects in creation.
rows.anchor: لا خبر عند العقول من كنه صفاته كما لا خبر عندها من كنه ذاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God is necessary; every possible thing depends on Him and remains under His ownership, power, and control, so He alone is one in acts.
rows.anchor: الممكن ما عداه وكل ما كان ممكنا فإنه يجوز أن لا يوجد ما لم يتصل بالواجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reflecting on divine decree reveals the meaning of 54:49, that God created everything according to a measure.
rows.anchor: قوله : { إنا كل شىء خلقناه بقدر } ( القمر : 49 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ilah means one who deserves worship, a relation that applies to all accountable people and to those who could become accountable.
rows.anchor: لما كان الإله هو يستحق أن يكون معبودا والذي يليق به أن يكون معبودا بهذا الوصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because ilah accepts possessive attribution, it means the worshipped deity, not merely the powerful one; the latter makes the phrase awkwardly say your powerful is one powerful.
rows.anchor: فلو كان معنى الإله القادر لصار المعنى وقادركم قادر واحد ومعلوم أنه ركيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word one after ilah specifies unity in divinity, rather than another respect of unity.
rows.anchor: ورود لفظ الواحد بعد لفظ الإله يدل على أن تلك الوحدة معتبرة في الإلهية لا في غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase no deity but Him removes the possible thought that our one deity differs from another people's deity, establishing unrestricted tawhid.
rows.anchor: هب أن إلهنا واحد ، فلعل إله غيرنا مغاير لإلهنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Negating the genus of deity excludes every individual of that genus; adding the exception then gives complete, universal tawhid.
rows.anchor: لا رجل يقتضي نفي هذه الماهية ، ومتى انتفت هذه الماهية انتفى جميع أفرادها

rows.speaker: جماعة من النحويين
rows.claim: Some grammarians posit ellipsis, supplying either no deity for us or no deity in existence before the exception.
rows.anchor: النحويين قالوا : الكلام فيه حذف وإضمار والتقدير : لا إله لنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Supplying for us narrows the claim to our deity and makes it repeat the preceding statement instead of affirming unrestricted tawhid.
rows.anchor: لكان هذا توحيدا لإلهنا لا توحيد للإله المطلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Supplying in existence avoids that repetition but merely denies a second deity's existence, weaker than the verse's denial of the deity-kind itself.
rows.anchor: كان هذا نفيا لوجود الإله الثاني ، أما لو لم يضمر هذا الإضمار كان قولك : لا إله إلا الله نفيا لماهية الإله الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unexpanded wording is stronger because denying the essence of deity gives purer tawhid than merely denying its existence.
rows.anchor: نفي الماهية أقوى في التوحيد الصرف من نفي الوجود ، فكان إجراء الكلام على ظاهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Negation of an essence is intelligible: if existence-ascription is separate, denying it denies that essence; if inseparable, negation returns to the essence or existence, so no ellipsis is needed.
rows.anchor: فإن كانت منفصلة عنهما كان نفيها نفيا لتلك الماهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although we conceive existence before nonexistence, the verse puts negation first to establish tawhid and deny partners and rivals.
rows.anchor: تقديم النفي على الإثبات كان لغرض إثبات التوحيد ونفي الشركاء والأنداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pronouns refer to speaker, addressee, or absent person without specifying a quiddity; al-Razi ranks أنا as most knowable, أنت next, and هو least.
rows.anchor: وأعرفها أنا ، ثم أنت ، ثم هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker knows himself without confusion, while speaker and addressee can be mistaken for others; the absent referent is least directly known.
rows.anchor: فالحاصل أن أشد المضمرات عرفانا { أنا } وأشدها بعدا عن العرفان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic first-person forms avoid gender distinctions when singular and share forms in the plural, since the speaker's identity is unambiguous.
rows.anchor: لفظ يستوي فيه المذكر والمؤنث من غير فصل ، لأن الفصل إنما يحتاج إليه عند الخوف من الإلتباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Second-person forms distinguish gender, number, and plurality because a speaker may address one of several present people and must prevent confusion.
rows.anchor: فصل بين لفظ مؤنثه ومذكره ، ويثني ويجمع ، لأنه قد يكون بحضرة المتكلم مؤنث ومذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Complete knowledge of God belongs only to God, who can refer to Himself by the most direct pronoun, أنا.
rows.anchor: فلما لم يكن لأحد أن يسير إلى تلك الحقيقة بالضمير الذي هو أعرف الضمائر وهو قول ( أنا ) إلا له سبحانه

rows.speaker: قوما يجوزون الاتحاد
rows.claim: Some allow union: a human spirit illuminated by knowledge of divine reality unites knower and known, letting the mystic say, I am God.
rows.anchor: قوما يجوزون الاتحاد : الأرواح البشرية إذا استنارت بأنوار معرفة تلك الحقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi rejects union as incoherent: if either party vanishes there is no union, and if both remain there are still two.
rows.anchor: إن فنيا أو أحدهما ، فذاك ليس باتحاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun أنت suits those present in unveiling and witnessing after they abandon human concerns and turn toward God.
rows.anchor: أما ( أنت ) فهو للحاضرين في مقامات المكاشفات والمشاهدات لمن فني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi says Yunus reached witnessing after being absent from created darkness; his prayer shows that direct witnessing and address require absence from all but God.
rows.anchor: على ما أخبر الله تعالى عن يونس عليه السلام أنه بعد أن فنى عن ظلمات عالم الحدوث

rows.speaker: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Muhammad says he cannot enumerate praise of God, who praises Himself as He deserves; al-Razi gives no grading here.
rows.anchor: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( لا أحصى ثناء عليك أنت كما أثنيت على نفسك )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun هو is used for the absent referent.
rows.anchor: وأما ( هو ) فللغائبين ، ثم ههنا بحث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Names are either universal, whose meanings permit sharing, or particular, whose referent excludes sharing; God is not captured by a universal concept.
rows.anchor: الإسم إما كلي أو جزئي ، وأعني بكلي أن يكون مفهومه بحيث لا يمنع تصوره من وقوع الشركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Derived names such as Merciful, Wise, Knowing, and Powerful do not by themselves designate God's unique essence; pronouns and demonstrative reference are more direct.
rows.anchor: جميع الأسماء المشتقة : كالرحمن ، والرحيم ، والحكيم ، والعليم ، والقادر ، لا يتناول ذاته المخصوصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since a simple, indivisible essence cannot be described or predicated of without introducing a distinction, هو alone reaches that essence and is nobler than other names.
rows.anchor: الفرد المطلق لا يمكن نعته ، لأن النعت يقتضي المغايرة بين الموصوف والصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Derived names direct attention to attributes known through created effects, making them a veil; هو signifies God as He is and cuts attention away from everything else.
rows.anchor: وأما ( هو ) فإنه لفظ يدل عليه من حيث هو هو لا من حيث عرضت له إضافة أو نسبة بالقياس إلى عالم الحدوث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the essence is the source of perfection and entails the attributes, هو reaches that source while other names stop at attributes; therefore هو is noblest.
rows.anchor: ولفظ ( هو ) يوصلك إلى ينبوع الرحمة والعزة والعلو وهو الذات وسائر الألفاظ لا توقفك إلا في مقامات النعوت والصفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammarians parse هو as nominative because it substitutes for the syntactic position of لا together with its noun.
rows.anchor: ارتفع ( هو ) لأنه بدل من موضع ( لا ) مع الاسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Substitution after negation turns the sentence into no one came except Zayd; in an affirmative sentence the same substitution would wrongly imply that everyone except Zayd came.
rows.anchor: البدلية هي الإعراض عن الأول والأخذ بالثاني فكأنك قلت : ما جاءني إلا زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For God, mercy means blessing: رحيم conveys abundant mercy, while الرحمن conveys its complete superlative degree, uniquely His.
rows.anchor: قلنا ( رحيم ) وإذا أردنا المبالغة التامة التي ليست إلا له سبحانه قلنا { الرحمان }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse follows exclusive divinity with the two mercy names to ease awe and signal that God's mercy precedes His anger and creation is for mercy and beneficence.
rows.anchor: إشعارا بأن رحمته سبقت غضبه وأنه ما خلق الخلق إلا للرحمة والإحسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, hajj means intending something repeatedly and continuing to visit it; hijja, with kasra, means a year because people perform pilgrimage annually.
rows.anchor: { الحج } في اللغة عبارة عن القصد وإنما يقال : حج فلان الشيء إذا قصده مرة بعد أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In law, hajj comprises specified acts classified as pillars, obligatory components whose omission is repaired by sacrifice, and sunnas whose omission incurs no sacrifice.
rows.anchor: فهو اسم لأفعال مخصوصة منها أركان ومنها أبعاض ومنها هيئات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi's school counts five hajj pillars: ihram, standing at Arafah, circumambulating the Kaaba, sa'i between Safa and Marwa, and shaving or shortening the hair.
rows.anchor: الأركان عندنا خمسة : الإحرام والوقوف بعرفة والطواف بالبيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On whether hair removal is a pillar, al-Razi prefers that it is a rite without which release from ihram does not occur.
rows.anchor: وفي حلق الرأس أو تقصيره قولان : أصحهما أنه نسك لا يحصل التحلل إلا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The listed obligatory components include entering ihram at the appointed boundary, remaining at Arafah until sunset according to one view, staying overnight at Muzdalifa before the sacrifice according to one view, stoning Aqaba, and Mina nights and stoning according to one view.
rows.anchor: الإحرام من الميقات والمقام بعرفة إلى المغرب في قول والبيتوتة بمزدلفة ليلة النحر في قول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other acts of hajj are sunnas.
rows.anchor: وأما سائر أعمال الحج فهي سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Umrah has four pillars: ihram, circumambulation, sa'i, and, under two opinions, shaving or shortening the hair.
rows.anchor: أركان العمرة فهي أربعة : الإحرام ، والطواف ، والسعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After sa'i, a pilgrim carrying an offering slaughters it and then shaves or shortens the hair, but release from ihram does not depend on slaughter.
rows.anchor: فإن كان معه هدي ذبحه ثم حلق أو قصر ، ولا يتوقف التحلل على ذبح الهدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi's school reads the command to complete hajj and umrah as unconditional: perform them fully, so umrah is obligatory.
rows.anchor: ذهب أصحابنا إلى أنه مطلق ، والمعنى : افعلوا الحج والعمرة على نعت الكمال والتمام

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa reads the command conditionally: whoever begins hajj or umrah must complete it, though beginning either was not itself obligatory.
rows.anchor: وهو قول أبي حنيفة رضي الله عنه : إن هذا الأمر مشروط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi says the disagreement makes umrah obligatory according to his school but nonobligatory according to Abu Hanifa.
rows.anchor: وفائدة هذا الخلاف أن العمرة واجبة عند أصحابنا ، وغير واجبة عن أبي حنيفة رحمه الله
